title: Reading a string copy's bounds
description: You can compare the source string's storage needs with the destination array.

steps.description: src contains hello and its terminating null character. You reserve only five characters in dest.

steps.question: Does dest have room for every character strcpy copies?
steps.answer: No. The five letters and terminating null character require six positions, so the copy exceeds dest's bounds.

steps.description: strcpy copies through the terminator before printf reads dest as a string. This out-of-bounds write gives the program undefined behavior.
The supplied recording prints Dest: hello and reaches the return. You can observe that output while still identifying the invalid copy from the array sizes.
